findings.title: The warning gives "unsafe method" as the reason, but retrylint flags non-idempotent methods, and PUT and DELETE, which RFC 9110 calls unsafe, are retried without a warning.
findings.problem: Safe (RFC 9110, section 9.2.1) and idempotent (section 9.2.2) are different sets. A reader of "unsafe" applies the wrong rule: they expect PUT and DELETE retries in the same file to be flagged, or remove them too. The golden files pin the wrong reason, so the suite now contradicts itself: put_delete_retry expects silence for two unsafe methods.

reproducer.code:
printf 'PUT /orders/42 5\nDELETE /orders/42 2\nPOST /orders 3\n' > c.conf
python3 -m retrylint c.conf
# current:  c.conf:3: POST /orders => retry x3 on an unsafe method; ...   (PUT and DELETE, also unsafe, not reported)
# expected: the POST warning names the property the check tests: POST is not idempotent

evidence.text: retrylint/messages.py:6: `f"{file}:{endpoint.line}: {endpoint.method} {endpoint.path} => retry x{endpoint.retries} on an unsafe method; "`

retrylint/__main__.py:7-9 and :16: "RFC 9110, section 9.2.2 defines GET, HEAD, OPTIONS, TRACE, PUT, and DELETE as idempotent", `IDEMPOTENT = {"GET", "HEAD", "OPTIONS", "TRACE", "PUT", "DELETE"}`, `if endpoint.retries > 0 and endpoint.method not in IDEMPOTENT`.

README.md:19-20: "it is only harmless for a method that RFC 9110 defines as idempotent (section 9.2.2) ... POST and PATCH are not idempotent." The function is named `non_idempotent_retry` (messages.py:4).

tests/golden/put_delete_retry.conf:1-3: "# PUT and DELETE are idempotent, so retrying them is fine.", PUT 5, DELETE 2; put_delete_retry.txt is empty. patch_retry.txt:1 and post_retry.txt:1 expect "on an unsafe method".
Run at 7463fb4 on PUT 5, DELETE 2, PURGE 1, POST 3: only PURGE and POST are reported, both "on an unsafe method"; exit 1.

The base text said "but {endpoint.method} is not idempotent (RFC 9110, section 9.2.2)" (messages.py:7 at 8587e48); the commit message gives brevity and ordering as the aim, not a change of the stated rule.

findings.proposed_solution: Update tests/golden/patch_retry.txt:1 and tests/golden/post_retry.txt:1 to match.
findings.suggestion: f"{file}:{endpoint.line}: {endpoint.method} {endpoint.path} => retry x{endpoint.retries} on a non-idempotent method; "
findings.retest: The warnings in tests/golden/post_retry.txt and patch_retry.txt say the method is not idempotent and do not contain "unsafe"; a method the RFCs do not list, such as `PURGE /cache 1`, gets the same wording, and put_delete_retry.conf still gives no warning.

findings.title: "Drop the retry policy." tells the user to remove the whole policy file, where the warning is about one endpoint's retries.
findings.problem: In this repository the retry policy is the whole file, including the GET and PUT retries the tool accepts. The change also drops the base text's Idempotency-Key alternative for a client that needs the retry, which the commit message does not mention.

evidence.text: retrylint/messages.py:7: `f"a retry may apply its effect twice. Drop the retry policy."`
README.md:3: "`retrylint` checks the retry policy of an HTTP client before it ships. A policy file lists one endpoint per line"; retrylint/policy.py:1: "Reads a retry policy file."
Base text (messages.py:8-9 at 8587e48): "Remove the retry, or send an Idempotency-Key header that the server deduplicates."
tests/golden/patch_retry.conf:2 `POST /payments 0` passes, so setting the endpoint's retries to 0 is the per-endpoint fix the tool accepts (__main__.py:16 `endpoint.retries > 0`).
retrylint does not read headers, so an endpoint that sends an Idempotency-Key is still reported; restoring that alternative needs a note that the warning stays.

findings.proposed_solution: Update both golden files to match. Whether to keep the Idempotency-Key alternative is the author's call; if it stays, say that retrylint still reports the endpoint.
findings.suggestion: f"a retry may apply its effect twice. Set this endpoint's retries to 0."
findings.retest: The remedy in the warnings for post_retry.conf and patch_retry.conf names the reported endpoint's retries (the `retries` column), not the retry policy or the policy file.

findings.title: Is one 80-column line the target? The shortened warning is still 136 and 141 characters, so it still wraps in the 80-column terminal the commit message names.
findings.problem: The change trades the stated reason and a remedy for length; if the goal is a line that does not wrap, the trade does not reach it, and the printed file path, given as typed, adds to every line.

evidence.text: Commit 7463fb4 body: "The warning wrapped over three lines in an 80-column terminal ... keep the message short enough to scan in a CI log."
Measured at 7463fb4: the warning line of patch_retry.conf renders 141 characters, post_retry.conf 136; at 8587e48 post_retry rendered 303.
retrylint/__main__.py:21-23 passes argv[1] as `file` into the message; tests/test_golden.py compares whole output text only, and no test bounds a line's length.

findings.retest: The author names the target. If it is one 80-column line, the golden warning lines fit in 80 characters; if two lines are enough, the question is settled with no change.

findings.title: "=> retry x3" replaces the policy's word "retries" with notation that can be read as three attempts in total.
findings.problem: The policy column counts retries after the first attempt, and HTTP clients count this setting both ways; the base text ("is retried up to 3 times") said which, "x3" does not, so a reader may set the value one off.

evidence.text: README.md:4: "how many times the client retries a failed request"; README.md:7 and tests/golden/post_retry.conf:1: "# method path retries"; retrylint/policy.py:11 `retries: int`.
tests/golden/post_retry.txt:1 renders "POST /orders => retry x3"; neither `=>` nor `x<n>` appears elsewhere in the repository at 8587e48.

findings.proposed_solution: Update both golden files to match.
findings.suggestion: f"{file}:{endpoint.line}: {endpoint.method} {endpoint.path} retried up to {endpoint.retries} times on an unsafe method; "
findings.retest: The warnings for post_retry.conf (count 3) and patch_retry.conf (count 2) state the count with the word "retries" or "retried" in a form that counts retries, not attempts, and contain no "x3" or "x2".

findings.title: The README describes the warning but never shows it, so a user holding the warning from a CI log cannot match it to the page.

evidence.text: README.md:18: "It prints one warning per endpoint whose retries can repeat a side effect, and exits with status 1 when it printed any." No example output follows; the change does not touch README.md.
git show 8587e48:README.md has the same text, so the page lacked the example before the change.

findings.proposed_solution: Show the output for the example policy at README.md:6-10 after the command at line 15, with the exit status, once the warning text is settled.
findings.retest: README.md shows the warning exactly as `python3 -m retrylint` prints it for the README's own example file.

findings.title: The commit message does not say what the new warning reads or that it drops the RFC reference and the Idempotency-Key remedy, which CI logs and scripts that grep the old text will see.

evidence.text: Commit 7463fb4 body: "The warning wrapped over three lines in an 80-column terminal, and the endpoint and the retry count sat in the middle of it. Put them first and keep the message short enough to scan in a CI log."
The diff removes "(RFC 9110, section 9.2.2)" and "send an Idempotency-Key header that the server deduplicates" from retrylint/messages.py.

findings.proposed_solution: Once the text is settled, quote the new warning for one endpoint in the body and name what it no longer carries.
findings.retest: The commit body quotes the warning as the final code emits it and names any content the old text had and the new one drops.
